newsitem.title: IRAQ: Turkish forces push into northern Iraq - witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Turkish forces push into northern Iraq - witnesses.

text.p: Turkish troops, backed by tanks and heavy artillery, pushed across the border into northern Iraq early on Wednesday in an apparent move against separatist Kurdish rebel bases, witnesses said.
The assault began at 3 a.m. (2300 GMT) and involved several thousand troops, the witnesses said. There were no immediate reports of any clashes.
"Three thousand troops, including tanks and artillery, started crossing at 2300 GMT and they are still continuing," a resident close to the border said.
Turkish army officers inside Iraq were tight-lipped, with one saying only: "We are here on exercises."

Earlier, local Kurdish authorities ordered all journalists to leave the border area and confiscated mobile telephones that could reach back into Turkey. Residents on the Turkish side said the border crossing at Habur was closed to all civilian traffic.

Turkish troops regularly cross back and forth in "hot pursuit" of rebels of the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK). In March of 1995, however, tens of thousands of troops pushed deep into Iraqi territory for a prolonged campaign.
